 JUDGMENT Challenging the award in M.V.C.No.6076/2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru (SCCH-24) C/c XXII Additional Small Causes Judge & Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore, the Managing Director of BMTC has preferred this appeal.
2. The appellant was the respondent and the respondents were the claimants before the Tribunal.

sentences.text: For the purpose of convenience, the parties will be referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the Tribunal.
3. Claimant No.1 is the wife, claimant Nos.2 and 3 are the minor children and claimant No.4 is the father of the deceased Rajesh Bhise.
4. On 27.08.2018 at 5.00 a.m. dead body of Rajesh Bhise was found lying in Kumaraswamy Layout at 15E bus stop within the limits of Kumaraswamy Traffic Police Station, Bangalore.
There were bleeding injuries on the dead body.
Regarding the incident, K.T.Krishnaiah, HC 4786 of Kumaraswamy Layout police station submitted his report as per Ex.P2.
It was pleaded in the complaint that between 4.00 a.m. to 6.00 a.m. some vehicle has hit the victim causing the accident and his consequential death.

sentences.text:
Based on the said complaint, Kumaraswamy Layout Traffic Police registered the first information report as per Ex.P1 in Crime No.138/2018 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304A of IPC and Sections 134 (a) &
(b) and 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'MV Act') against unknown person.

On investigation, the police filed charge sheet as per Ex.P10 alleging that on 27.08.2018 at 5.00 a.m. the driver of bus bearing registration No.KA-57- F-2680 negligently hit the deceased in the bus stop and consequently the victim fell under the rear wheel of the vehicle, suffered injuries and died.
6.

The claimants filed claim petition before the Tribunal claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/-
on the ground that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence of the driver of the bus and due to the death of the victim they have lost their breadwinner.
7. The respondent-Managing Director of BMTC contested the petition denying actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.

The respondent contended that the deceased himself was negligently sleeping under the parked bus and in the morning when the driver tried to move the bus without noticing the deceased, the deceased came under the rear wheel of the bus.
Therefore the deceased himself was responsible for the accident.

8. The Tribunal on recording the evidence of the claimants and on hearing the parties, by the impugned award held that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.

The Tribunal relying on Ex.P16 transfer certificate of the deceased, considered his age at 46, notionally assessed his income at Rs.12,500/- per month, added 25% of the same by way of future prospects, deducted 1/4th of the same for his personal expenses, applied 15 multiplier and awarded compensation of Rs.21,09,420/- on the head of loss of dependency.

9. The Tribunal in all awarded compensation of Rs.23,03,300/- on different heads as follows:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 21,09,420/-
 2. Transportation, medical 17,000/-
 and funeral expenses  3. Loss of estate 17,000/-
 4. Loss of consortium 1,60,000/-

Total 23,03,420/-
 rounded to

Submissions of Sri D.Vijayakumar, learned Counsel for BMTC:
10.
The accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased himself and the finding of the Tribunal on that point is unsustainable.
The multiplier applied is incorrect.

Submissions of Sri A.S.Girish,
learned Counsel for the claimants:

sentences.text: On investigation the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the bus.

To rebut the document,
the BMTC did not examine the driver of the bus.
Therefore the finding of the Tribunal on the point of rashness and negligence does not call for any interference.
The compensation awarded on all heads is justifiable.

Reg. Negligence:
12.
As per the claimant's own document the dead body was found lying and the matter was reported by the police and not by any of the alleged eyewitnesses.

The accident occurred between 4.00 a.m.
and 6.00 a.m.
The claimants and the Tribunal both relied on Exs.P3 and P4, the statements of alleged eyewitnesses in the charge sheet.
Such statements are inadmissible in evidence having regard to Section 32 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
If those persons were eyewitnesses then they would have reported the matter to the police.
Therefore the finding of the Tribunal by placing reliance on Exs.P3 and P4 that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the driver of the bus is erroneous.
13. However, the respondent itself in its statement of objections admitted the involvement of the bus.
But the contention of the respondent-BMTC was that the deceased himself came under rear wheel of the bus by sleeping under the bus.
To establish the said defence, even BMTC did not examine the driver of the bus.
However, the charge sheet itself states that rear wheel of the bus ran over the deceased.
That goes to show that the deceased came under rear wheel of the bus and it was not the case of the driver of the bus hitting the deceased directly.
That goes to show that to some extent the deceased also contributed to the accident.
Therefore 20% of the negligence can be imputed to the deceased himself with reference to the accident.

Reg. Quantum of compensation:
14.

So far as the compensation payable, since the claimants did not produce any proof of actual income of the deceased, the Tribunal was justified in assessing his income notionally at Rs.12,500/-
per month.
The Tribunal considering the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi1 has added 25% of the same by way of future prospects.

sentences.text: 15. The deceased was aged 46 years.
Therefore as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation2 the applicable multiplier is 13.

entities.text: Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal committed error in taking the multiplier of 15.
Since the deceased had four dependants, 1/4th of the income deducted for his personal expenses is AIR 2017 SC 5157 AIR 2009 SC 3104 justifiable.

Therefore, the compensation payable on the head of loss of dependency comes to (Rs.12,500 x 25%
of 12,500 x = 11719 x 12 x 13)=18,28,164/-.
16.
The compensation awarded on the head of consortium, loss of estate, funeral expenses is in accordance with the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case referred to supra.

Therefore just compensation payable is as follows:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in  Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 18,28,164/-
 2. Loss of Consortium 1,60,000/-

sentences.text:
In view of the finding with regard to rashness and negligence on the part of the deceased at 20%,
the claimants are entitled to 80% of the amount by way of compensation which comes to (Rs.20,22,164/- x 80%) Rs.16,17,731.20/-.
The appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence the following:
ORDER
The appeal is partly allowed.

The impugned award of the Tribunal is modified as follows:
(i) The claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.16,17,731/- with interest thereon at 6% per annum from the date of the petition till its realization.
(ii) The appellant/BMTC shall deposit the said amount before the Tribunal, after adjusting the amount already deposited if any, within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this award.

(iii) The order of the Tribunal with regard to apportionment and investment is maintained.
(iv) Registry shall transmit the amount in deposit if any and the trial Court records to the Tribunal forthwith.
Sd/-
